Ligand 1 has the best synthetic accessibility I have seen this run (SA 1.80) and already carries a diaryl urea, which is a spine that shows up across kinase inhibitor series - worth keeping rather than crossing away. Ligand 2 is a tert-amyl benzamide/urea with SA 2.97 and no activity; nothing to take from it. Every probe so far has installed a single hinge binder on an otherwise ZINC-like scaffold, and a fingerprint classifier may well still read those as inactive because most of the molecule is unremarkable. So this episode tests stacking two recognized features instead of one: keep the urea and add an anilinopyrimidine. The primary acetamide at atoms 15-18 is the right thing to sacrifice - it costs 2 donors and a lot of TPSA (currently 102.7) and contributes nothing. Cut the non-ring aryl-CH2 bond 14-15 and attach N-linked pyrimidin-2-ylamino, turning that ring into a 4-(pyrimidin-2-ylamino)phenyl.
